line-strong.purpose: Every boundary that identifies a control; at least 3.20:1 on every surface.

cta-base.purpose: Base of the one gradient on the site, on the closing CTA panel only.

photo-scrim.purpose: Flat, never a gradient. Holds on-photo text at 5.78:1 over any frame in the library.

display.purpose: The page h1 only, one per page, capped at two lines and balanced.

title.purpose: Card and bento-cell h3, measure capped around 22ch.

body.purpose: All running copy at 16px / 1.6; lead copy steps up to 1.125rem.

label.purpose: Buttons, nav links (15px), form labels. The single eyebrow is 0.75rem / 0.06em / uppercase in muted ink.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Resting material for every card, cell, panel and device frame. Tinted to the page hue, never black.

shadows.name: card-dark
shadows.purpose: Same role in dark mode; the inset highlight resolves the card edge without a heavy border.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Hover on something clickable, and the hero image at rest. Never on a static surface.

shadows.name: nav-inset
shadows.purpose: Top highlight on the floating glass nav, over the card shadow.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: CSS sampling of the contract spring (stiffness 100, damping 20): critically damped, settles in about 600ms.

motion.name: spring-content
motion.purpose: Motion default for entrances and layout changes; 60ms stagger across a grid.

motion.name: spring-thumb
motion.purpose: Segmented-control and tab thumb: lands in about 250ms with no overshoot.

motion.name: hover-shadow
motion.purpose: The only hover transition on a card; nothing moves.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: Entrance for headline words (40ms stagger) and in-view cells, on ease-spring.

narrative.overview:
Someone arrives here because their site is down. The design answers by looking like a room where this is handled every day: a composed board of everything that can break, each area a card with its own weight, nothing flashing, nothing shouting. The surfaces are cool paper greys that sit a hair apart in tone; the type is confident without being loud; and exactly one colour, a deep functional green, marks the thing the visitor came for. That restraint is the whole trick. If three things competed for the signal, nothing would read as under control.

Depth is soft rather than dramatic. Every card rests on a two-layer shadow tinted to the background's cool hue (around hue 220), never black, so the board looks lit rather than cut out. Corners are generous (20px on anything card-shaped), controls are full pills, and the single translucent surface on the entire site is the floating nav. Photography is bright daylight and literal: a desk, a laptop, a shop owner checking orders. Where the subject is a WordPress error, the image is a real capture from public/screens/, not a div dressed up as a browser. Evidence beats illustration here, because the product claim is competence.

Motion reports, it does not perform. Cells rise 12px and fade as the grid comes into view, in reading order; a toggle's thumb slides to the option you picked; a button presses 2%. Everything runs on one critically damped spring (stiffness 100, damping 20) and collapses to its final state under reduced motion. The world this rejects is specific and confirmed: no second accent, no brand red, no glass beyond the nav, no gradients beyond one closing panel, no GSAP, no marquees, no parallax, no neon.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, used as a signal, on a cool paper grey field
Bento board layout with deliberately unequal spans
Soft two-layer shadows tinted to the background hue, never black
Three radii only: 20px cards, 12px fields, full-pill controls
Both themes designed, not inverted, and every pair measured at AA
Real photographs and real error captures; no synthetic UI
Spring motion on transform and opacity only

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: One accent, and it means "back online". The brand red (#CC3333 in brand.accent) does not appear anywhere in this variation: it competes with the signal and reads as an error state. No second hue gets introduced to mark a highlighted plan, a badge, or a state.

rules.name: The Control Boundary Rule
rules.body: --line is decorative and measures 1.24:1. Any boundary that identifies something operable (input, select, checkbox, segmented track) uses --line-strong, which measures at least 3.20:1 on every surface in both themes.

rules.name: The Accent-On-Light Rule
rules.body: Small accent-coloured text sits on --surface (4.89:1) or --bg (4.56:1), never on --surface-2, where it drops to 4.31:1. On that surface the accent is for large text and icons only.

rules.name: The Display-Never-Body Rule
rules.body: Cabinet Grotesk sets headings and the wordmark. It never sets running copy, labels, or UI text, at any size.

rules.name: The Muted-Not-Faded Rule
rules.body: Secondary text uses --muted, never reduced opacity on --text. Opacity breaks the measured contrast and goes grey-on-grey over photographs.

rules.name: The Tightening Rule
rules.body: Display tracking closes to -0.02em from 48px up; body and label tracking stay at normal. Nothing in this system is letterspaced for decoration except the single uppercase eyebrow.

rules.name: The No-Three-Equal-Cards Rule
rules.body: No row of three equal cards, anywhere. On the board, spans vary so no row reads as a tidy triptych; every cell is fully readable at rest, without hover.

rules.name: The Floating-Nav Clearance Rule
rules.body: html carries scroll-padding-top: 6rem and scroll-padding-bottom: 6.5rem (dropping to 2rem at 768px) so no anchor target or keyboard tab stop ever parks under the floating nav or the mobile action bar.

rules.name: The Lift-Means-Link Rule
rules.body: --shadow-lift on hover says "this is clickable". A non-interactive surface never grows its shadow, and an interactive one never changes size or position on hover; the transition is box-shadow only, so nothing in the grid shifts.

rules.name: The No-Black-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted to the page hue (220), never rgba(0,0,0,...). Black shadows read as dirt on a cool grey field.

rules.name: The Three-Radius Rule
rules.body: 20 / 12 / pill. A new radius is a bug, not a variation.

rules.name: The Transform-And-Opacity Rule
rules.body: Animate transform and opacity only, on the spring (stiffness 100, damping 20) with a 60ms stagger across a grid, and let useReducedMotion() collapse every one of them to its final state. Hover scale, where it exists, sits on a wrapper so it cannot shift layout.

dos: Do keep the accent scarce and functional: fills, the thumb, the focus ring, accent text. If a screen has accent in more than a few places, something that is not a signal is wearing the signal.
Do use --line-strong on every control boundary and --line only for decoration.
Do design both themes. Check any new pair against the measured table in design-system/letsfixwp-v3/MASTER.md rather than assuming the dark value inverts.
Do keep to 20 / 12 / pill, and to --shadow-card / --shadow-lift.
Do ship real imagery: daylight photography from src/content/photos.ts (never a red-toned frame in this variation) or real captures from public/screens/, inside the device frame.
Do mark unconfirmed content visibly, with the dashed --line-strong placeholder frame, rather than letting a placeholder pass as fact.
Do give every animation a one-sentence job (hierarchy, feedback, state) and a reduced-motion collapse.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent, brand red #CC3333, or any extra hue for a badge, a highlighted plan, or a state.
Don't use glass anywhere except the floating nav, or a gradient anywhere except the closing CTA mesh.
Don't use pure #000000 or #FFFFFF, or rgba(0,0,0,...) shadows.
Don't set body copy in Cabinet Grotesk, or fade text with opacity instead of --muted.
Don't put small accent-coloured text on --surface-2.
Don't add GSAP, marquees, parallax, scroll listeners, custom cursors, or neon glows.
Don't build a row of three equal cards, a fake screenshot or dashboard from divs, or put a pill or label on top of an image.
Don't let a hover change layout, or leave a focus state invisible.
